canonical_policy.name: Correctness and clarity before optimization
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Prefer clear correct code first; do not introduce specialized optimizations without a concrete reason and prefer measurement/profiling for non-trivial optimization.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Clear correct code first and measure nontrivial optimization matches canonical; EXTRA0095 lazy loading first and no custom Angular optimization without real need, 0211 material improvement verification, and0392 credible performance review already registered.

context_quotes:
Prefer clear, correct code first. Do not introduce specialized performance
optimizations without a concrete reason; for non-trivial optimizations, prefer
measurement or profiling evidence over assumptions.

These techniques are valid, but by default introduce them only for a measured
or clearly demonstrated need: compiled queries, `ValueTask<T>`,
`ArrayPool<T>`/`MemoryPool<T>`, manual object pooling, custom serialization
optimizations, aggressive caching, and raw SQL for performance. Do not
sacrifice maintainability for speculative micro-optimization.

Prefer ordinary clear .NET code. For demonstrated allocation-heavy hot paths,
consider spans, pooling, source-generated serialization, or preallocated
buffers, and verify that the optimization materially improves the workload.

Do not prematurely optimize normal Angular code. Use route lazy loading and
sensible rendering and data access first; introduce memoization, virtual
scrolling, custom change-detection work, or other optimizations after
identifying a real need.

Report performance concerns only with a credible reason — obvious N+1 access,
unbounded materialization, repeated expensive external calls, blocking async
I/O, obvious high-volume allocation in a demonstrated hot path. Do not
recommend caching, compiled queries, pooling, `ValueTask`, or similar
optimizations speculatively.

Start with clear LINQ and optimize after identifying a real problem. Inspect
database round trips, selected columns, N+1 behavior, indexes, generated SQL,
the query plan where necessary, materialized data volume, and tracking
overhead before introducing specialized optimization.

`Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, stack allocation, and pooling are performance
tools. Use ordinary arrays, strings, and collections by default and introduce
these only when profiling or a clearly hot path justifies the complexity
(`performance.md` § Allocation-Sensitive Code).

canonical_policy.name: Database access is efficient by default
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Filter/project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips/over-fetching/N+1 patterns, and paginate potentially large result sets.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Practical database filter/project, N+1 avoidance and pagination covered. Entity-needed exception0450, tracking/no-tracking DTO limits EXTRA0146, explicit shape/split query verification EXTRA0147, always deterministic ordering EXTRA0148/BF0097 and inspection before optimizing0460 separately registered.

context_quotes:
Keep database work efficient by default: filter and project in the database
when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips and loading significantly more
data than required, watch for N+1 query patterns, and paginate potentially
large result sets.

For read-only queries that need selected data, prefer database-side
projection:

Projection is not mandatory when the use case genuinely needs the entity; avoid
loading a complete aggregate only to return two scalar fields.

Use tracking queries when loaded entities will be modified and committed
through the current Unit of Work. Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only entity
queries where change tracking provides no value; do not add it mechanically to
projections that already produce non-entity DTOs.

Prefer an explicit query shape: projection when only selected related data is
needed, `Include`/`ThenInclude` when the entity graph itself is required. Avoid
lazy loading by default because it hides database access and causes N+1
queries. For large collection includes, consider split queries and verify the
generated SQL and performance.

Apply filtering, ordering, and pagination in the database, always with a
deterministic order:

```csharp
var query = db.Orders
    .Where(x => x.CustomerId == customerId)
    .OrderByDescending(x => x.CreatedAt);

var totalCount = await query.CountAsync(cancellationToken);

var items = await query
    .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
    .Take(pageSize)
    .Select(x => new OrderSummary(
        x.Id,
        x.Total,
        x.CreatedAt))
    .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);
```

operation; all rows loaded and filtered in memory; lazy loading by default;

existing database, or left stale after a model change.

| Scenario | Default |
|---|---|
| Use-case persistence dependency | Specific repository interface |
| Commit application changes | `IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` |
| Repository implementation | EF Core inside the adapter layer |
| Read-only entity query | `AsNoTracking()` when useful |
| Read model | Database-side projection |
| Primary-key entity lookup | `FindAsync` when its semantics fit |
| Complex entity graph | Explicit `Include` / projection |
| Set-based mass update/delete | `ExecuteUpdateAsync` / `ExecuteDeleteAsync` when appropriate |
| Measured extremely hot query | Consider a compiled query |
| Multiple commits requiring atomicity | Explicit transaction |
| Production schema change | Reviewed migration / controlled deployment |
| Empty development database | Run the maintained development seeder |
| Existing development database | Leave seed data unchanged |
| Need a fresh local seed dataset | Recreate the local database explicitly |
| Test data | Dedicated test setup, not development seeding |

canonical_policy.name: Caching requires concrete semantics/need
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Caching is not a default architecture requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured/reasoned need and choose implementation according to deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Reasoned need, deployment and stale-data costs match. Define consistency first and measure before caching solely for performance0357 already express ordering and performance trigger; no cache merely for frequency.

context_quotes:
- Caching is an optimization, not a default architectural requirement.
  Introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need — measured expensive
  repeated work, high read volume, expensive remote calls — with acceptable
  staleness semantics, and choose the implementation according to deployment,
  consistency, and staleness requirements. Do not cache merely because a value
  is read frequently.
- Every cache entry must have a lifetime or another explicit invalidation

Define consistency semantics first — how stale data may become and how it is
invalidated — and measure before adding caching solely for performance.

Add a distributed backend such as Redis only when deployment requirements
justify it (distributed caching is Reserved).

Decide whether a cache failure falls back to the source, fails the request, or
returns stale data.

Check-by-reference against `performance.md` § Caching and `architecture.md`
§ Layer Placement: caching by default without a reason; global keys for
tenant/user data; mutable data cached indefinitely without invalidation; cache
technology in Domain; Application depending directly on `HybridCache` without a
deliberate decision; tracked persistence entities cached across Unit of Work
boundaries; cache used as authoritative persistence; Redis added merely because
the application caches.

| Need | Default consideration |
|---|---|
| Entire reusable HTTP response | ASP.NET Core output caching |
| Local application cache | In-memory or HybridCache |
| Multi-instance shared cache | Distributed cache / HybridCache L2 |
| Expensive repeated remote read | Cache in Infrastructure when the contract permits |
| Application-controlled invalidation | Application abstraction + Infrastructure implementation |
| Unknown performance problem | Measure before adding caching |
